dedupe_keys.name: automation induced reshoring agent based model of the german manufacturing industry netlogo comses

description: An agent-based model of how German manufacturing firms decide whether to bring offshore production back home as automation spreads. The CoMSES record says firms follow simple economic rules at the micro level and respond to a changing environment, and that experiments varying initial conditions showed stricter environmental rules on global trade and rising wages in former offshore locations to be the main drivers and brakes of relocation, with a shift from purely economic reasons towards sustainability. Version 1.0.0 was submitted by Laura Merz, published on 20 November 2020 and last modified on 5 December 2024, and is a free download under the MIT licence. The record notes that with many ticks the revenue term overflows the numbers NetLogo can handle, so the model is volatile. Coverage is the German manufacturing sector as a stylised system. Caveats: a stylised model with no calibration data named on the page read, and numerical instability over long runs. For simulation it lets planners explore how reshoring changes where industrial demand for power, freight and labour will sit, and how supply chains respond to shocks abroad. Related catalogue records include the industrial symbiosis network implementation ABM on CoMSES.
